calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Oilers
calls.body: The Oilers’ power play is the league’s best, and the Kraken’s kill is one of the league’s worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Kraken more than most.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.7 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Edmonton 1st for power play (9.7 expected goals per 60) · Seattle 29th for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Edmonton’s power play created 6.2 expected goals per 60 in 5:06 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 9.7, and scored 0 goals.

calls.head: The Oilers can’t afford to cough it up
calls.body: The Kraken turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Oilers are one of the league’s worst at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Oilers.
calls.call: The Kraken get at least their usual 7.5% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
calls.nums: Seattle 10th for chances off turnovers (7.5% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · Edmonton 29th for avoiding breakdowns
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: 0.6% of Seattle’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against their usual 7.5%.

calls.head: Sheltered against exposed
calls.body: The Kraken are one of the league’s best for preventing dangerous shots, at the sheltered end; the Oilers are one of the league’s worst, at the exposed end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Kraken prevent dangerous shots better than the Oilers do.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average shot allowed was, Seattle had 7.7% a shot and Edmonton 6.2% a shot. Coming in, Seattle was at 6.0% a shot and Edmonton at 6.7% a shot.
calls.usual: SEA 6.0% a shot · EDM 6.7% a shot
calls.tonight: SEA 7.7% a shot · EDM 6.2% a shot

EDM.head: We gave Edmonton a 73% chance, and Edmonton delivered.

SEA.head: We gave Seattle only a 27% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Seattle hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Seattle’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 61, against their usual 113 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

surprises.head: Edmonton shortened their bench
surprises.body: Edmonton’s bottom-six forwards played 38% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 41% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 7 games.

story.head: The Oilers beat the Kraken
paras: Owen Michaels opened the scoring early in the first. Leon Draisaitl scored the winner late in the third.
The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Oilers win about four in five.

items.text: None of the preview’s three calls held.
